children.text: oṃ namo maṅgalamūrtaye |
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutations to the Auspicious One (<s>Maṅgalamūrti</s>)!

children.text: atha pratyabhijñāhṛdayam || [1]
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam</s> (The Heart of Recognition). || [1]

children.text: namaḥ śivāya satataṃ pañcakṛtyavidhāyine |
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>, who eternally performs the fivefold act (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>),

children.text: cidānandaghanasvātmaparamārthāvabhāsine || [2]
children.translated_text: who causes the supreme reality of His own Self — a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>) — to shine forth. || [2]

children.text: śāṅkaropaniṣatsārapratyabhijñāmahodadheḥ |
children.translated_text: From the great ocean of the [doctrine of] Recognition (<s>Pratyabhijñā</s>), which is the essence of the <s>Śaiva Upaniṣads</s>,

children.text: kṣemeṇoddhṛyate sāraḥ saṃsāraviṣaśāntaye ||
children.translated_text: the essence is drawn out by <s>Kṣema[rāja]</s>, for the pacification of the poison of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).

children.text:
iha ye sukumāramatayo 'kṛtatīkṣṇatarkaśāstrapariśramāḥ
śaktipātonmiṣitapārameśvarasamāveśābhilāṣiṇaḥ katicit bhaktibhājaḥ
teṣām īśvarapratyabhijñopadeśatattvaṃ manāk unmīlyate | tatra
svātmadevatāyā eva sarvatra kāraṇatvaṃ sukhopāyaprāpyatvaṃ mahāphalatva.=
m
ca abhivyaṅktum āha
children.translated_text: Here, for those few devotees of tender intellect, who have not undergone the exertion of rigorous logical treatises (<s>tarka-śāstra</s>), [but] who aspire to the immersion in the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara-samāveśa</s>) that has been opened by the descent of [divine] power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) — for them, the essential truth of the teaching of <s>Īśvara-pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord) is briefly revealed here. Therein, in order to make manifest that the deity who is one's own Self is the cause of everything, is attainable by easy means, and yields the highest fruit, he says:

children.text: citiḥ svatantrā viśvasiddhihetuḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>Citi</s>), [being] autonomous (<s>svatantrā</s>), is the cause of the accomplishment of the universe. || Sūtra 1 ||

children.text:
viśvasya sadāśivādeḥ bhūmyantasya siddhau niṣpattau prakāśane
sthityātmani parapramātṛviśrāntyātmani ca saṃhāre parāśaktirūpā citir
eva bhagavatī svatantrā anuttaravimarśamayī śivabhaṭṭārakābhinnā hetuḥ
kāraṇam | asyāṃ hi prasarantyāṃ jagat unmiṣati vyavatiṣṭhate ca
nivṛttaprasarāyāṃ ca nimiṣati iti svānubhava eva atra sākṣī |
anyasya tu māyāprakṛtyādeḥ citprakāśabhinnasya aprakāśamānatvena
asattvān na kvacid api hetutvam prakāśamānatve tu prakāśaikātmyāt
prakāśarūpā citir eva hetuḥ na tv asau kaścit |
ata eva deśakālākārā etatsṛṣṭā etadanuprāṇitāś ca naitatsvarūpaṃ
bhettum alam iti vyāpakanityoditaparipūrṇarūpā iyam ity arthalabhyam eva
etat | nanu jagad api cito bhinnaṃ naiva kiṃcit abhede ca kathaṃ
hetuhetumadbhāvaḥ ucyate | cid eva bhagavatī svacchasvatantrarūpā
tattadanantajagadātmanā sphurati ity etāvat paramārtho 'yaṃ
kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ | yataś ca iyam eva pramātṛpramāṇaprameyamayasya
viśvasya siddhau prakāśane hetuḥ tato 'syāḥ
svatantrāparicchinnasvaprakāśarūpāyāḥ siddhau abhinavārthaprakāśanarūpa.=
m
na pramāṇavarākam upayuktam upapannaṃ vā |
tad uktam trikasāre
children.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>citi</s>) — the Blessed One, having the form of the Supreme Power (<s>Parā Śakti</s>), consisting of the supreme reflective awareness (<s>anuttara-vimarśa</s>), non-different from the Lord <s>Śiva</s> — She alone, being autonomous (<s>svatantrā</s>), is the cause, i.e., the reason, for the accomplishment — that is, the bringing forth, the manifestation — of the universe from <s>Sadāśiva</s> down to the earth, [including] its maintenance — whose nature is [continued] existence — and its dissolution, whose nature is repose in the Supreme Knower (<s>para-pramātṛ</s>). For when She expands, the world unfolds and persists; and when She has ceased to expand, [the world] closes — one's own experience itself is the witness here. But for anything else — <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, etc. — since it is different from the light of consciousness, it does not shine [independently], and being non-existent [in that sense], it is in no case a cause. And if it does shine, then, due to its identity with luminosity alone, it is consciousness (<s>citi</s>) in the form of luminosity that is the cause — not that [inert entity] at all. Therefore, space, time, and form — being created by Her and enlivened by Her — are not capable of breaking Her essential nature. Thus it follows implicitly that She is all-pervading, eternally arisen, and of complete fullness. Objection: If the universe is not at all different from consciousness, then how can there be a cause-effect relationship in the absence of difference? [Reply:] It is said: The blessed consciousness (<s>citi</s>), in Her transparent and autonomous form, flashes forth as the Self of each and every infinite universe — this much alone is the ultimate meaning of the cause-effect relationship. And since She alone is the cause of the accomplishment — i.e., the manifestation — of the universe consisting of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), therefore, for the establishment of Her — who is autonomous, unlimited, and self-luminous — the wretched means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is neither useful nor appropriate. As stated in the <s>Trikasāra</s>:

children.text:
svapadā svaśiraśchāyāṃ yadval laṅghitum īhate |
pādoddeśe śiro na syāt tatheyaṃ baindavī kalā || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Just as one tries to jump over the shadow of one's own head with one's own feet — the foot cannot reach where the head is — so is this <s>Baindavī Kalā</s> (the power of the Point).' //

children.text:
yataś ca iyaṃ viśvasya siddhau parādvayasamārasyāpādanātmani ca saṃhare
hetuḥ tata eva svatantrā | pratyabhijñātasvātantryā satī
bhogamokṣasvarūpāṇāṃ viśvasiddhīnāṃ hetuḥ |
ity āvṛttyā vyākhyeyam | api ca viśvaṃ nīlasukhadehaprāṇādi tasya yā
siddhiḥ pramānopārohakrameṇa vimarśamayapramātrāveśaḥ saiva hetuḥ
parijñāne upāyo yasyāḥ | anena ca sukhopāyatvam uktam | yad uktaṃ
śrīvijñānabhaṭṭārake
children.translated_text: And since She is the cause of the accomplishment of the universe and also of its dissolution — whose nature is the establishment of unity with the Supreme Non-dual [Reality] — therefore [She is called] autonomous (<s>svatantrā</s>). When Her autonomy has been recognized, She becomes the cause of all accomplishments of the universe in the form of [worldly] enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Thus [the sūtra] should be explained repeatedly. Moreover: the universe — blue [objects], pleasure, body, vital breath, etc. — its 'accomplishment' (<s>siddhi</s>) is the immersion in the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) who consists of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), through the progressive ascent of the means of knowledge — that itself is the cause, i.e., the means, for the complete understanding [of reality]. By this, the attainability by easy means is stated. As said in the venerable <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām |
yogināṃ tu viśeṣo 'yaṃ saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā [3] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The awareness of grasped and grasper is common to all embodied beings; but the distinction for yogins is this: attentiveness in [that] connection.' //

children.text:
citiḥ iti ekavacanaṃ deśakālādyanavacchinnatām abhidadhat
samastabhedavādānām avāstavatāṃ vyanakti | svatantraśabdo
brahmavādavailakṣaṇyam ācakṣāṇaḥ cito māheśvaryasāratāṃ brūte |
children.translated_text: The word '<s>svatantra</s>' (autonomous), declaring the distinctness from the <s>Brahman</s>-doctrine [of the Vedāntins], proclaims that the essence of consciousness is [Her] supreme sovereignty (<s>Māheśvarya</s>).

children.text: viśva ityādipadam aśeṣaśaktitvaṃ sarvakāraṇatvaṃ sukhopāyatvaṃ
children.translated_text: The term beginning with '<s>viśva</s>' (universe) states [Her] possession of all powers, [Her] being the cause of everything, [Her] attainability by easy means,

children.text: mahāphalaṃ ca āha ||
children.translated_text: and the greatness of the fruit. ||
The singular number in '<s>citiḥ</s>' (consciousness), by expressing [Her] non-limitation by space, time, etc., reveals the unreality of all doctrines of difference.

children.text:
nanu viśvasya yadi citiḥ hetuḥ tat asyā upādānādyapekṣāyāṃ
bhedavādāparityāgaḥ syāt
ity āśaṅkya āha
children.translated_text: Now, if consciousness is the cause of the universe, then — if She requires a material cause and the like — the doctrine of difference would not be abandoned. Anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text: svecchayā svabhittau viśvam unmīlayati || 2 ||
children.translated_text: By Her own will (<s>svecchā</s>), She unfolds the universe upon Her own screen (<s>svabhitti</s>). || Sūtra 2 ||

children.text:
svecchayā na tu brahmādivad anyecchayā | tayaiva ca na tu upādānādyapekṣay=
ā
| evaṃ hi prāguktasvātantryahānyā cittvam eva na ghaṭeta | svabhittau na
tu anyatra kvāpi | prāk nirṇītaṃ viśvaṃ darpaṇe nagaravat abhinnam api
bhinnam iva unmīlayati | unmīlanaṃ ca avasthitasyaiva prakaṭīkaraṇaṃ it=
y
anena jagataḥ prakaśaikātmyenāvasthānam uktam ||
children.translated_text: By Her own will — not, like <s>Brahmā</s> and others, by another's will. And by that [will] alone — not by dependence on a material cause etc. For otherwise, if the previously stated autonomy were lost, [Her] very nature as consciousness would be impossible. 'Upon Her own screen' — not anywhere else. She unfolds the universe — previously established [as non-different from Her] — like a city in a mirror, [which is] non-different yet appears as if different. And the 'unfolding' (<s>unmīlana</s>) is the making manifest of what already exists — by this, the abiding of the universe in identity with luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) is stated. ||

children.text: atha viśvasya svarūpaṃ vibhāgena pratipādayitum āha
children.translated_text: Now, in order to set forth the nature of the universe in its divisions, he says:

children.text: tan nānā anurūpagrāhyagrāhakabhedāt || 3 ||
children.translated_text: That [universe] is manifold, due to the differentiation of mutually adapted objects and subjects. || Sūtra 3 ||

children.text:
tad viśvaṃ nānā anekaprakāram | katham anurūpāṇāṃ
parasparaucityāvasthīnāṃ grāhyāṇāṃ grāhakāṇāṃ ca bhedād vaicitryāt |
tathā ca sadāśivatattve 'hantācchāditāsphuṭedantāmayaṃ yādṛśaṃ
parāpararūpaṃ viśvaṃ grāhyaṃ tādṛg eva
śrīsadāśivabhaṭṭārakādhiṣṭhito mantramaheśvarākhyaḥ pramātṛvargaḥ
parameśvarecchāvakalpitatathāvasthānaḥ |
īśvaratattve sphuṭedantāhantāsāmānādhikaraṇyātma yādṛg viśvaṃ grāhya.=
m
tathāvidha eva īśvarabhaṭṭārakādhiṣṭhito mantreśvaravargaḥ |
vidyāpade śrīmadanantabhaṭṭārakādhiṣṭhitā bahuśākhāvāntarabhedabhinnā
yathābhūtā mantrāḥ pramātāraḥ tathābhūtam eva bhedaikasāraṃ viśvam api
prameyam | māyordhve yādṛśā vijñānākalāḥ
kartṛtāśūnyaśuddhabodhātmānaḥ tādṛg eva tadabhedasāraṃ
sakalapralayākalātmakapūrvāvasthāparicitam eṣāṃ prameyam | māyāyāṃ
śūnyapramātṝṇāṃ pralayakevalināṃ svocitaṃ pralīnakalpaṃ prameyam |
kṣitiparyantāvasthitānāṃtu sakalānāṃ sarvato bhinnānāṃ parimitānāṃ
tathābhūtam eva prameyam | taduttīrṇaśivabhaṭṭārakasya
prakāśaikavapuṣaḥ prakāśaikarūpā eva bhāvāḥ | śrīmatparamaśivasya
punaḥ viśvottīrṇaviśvātmakaparamānandamayaprakāśaikaghanasya
evaṃvidham eva śivādidharaṇyantam akhilaṃ abhedenaiva sphurati | na tu
vastutaḥ anyat kiṃcit grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ vā | api tu
śrīparamaśivabhaṭṭāraka eva itthaṃ nānāvaicitryasahasraiḥ sphuratīty
abhihitaprāyam ||
children.translated_text: That universe is manifold — of many kinds. How? Due to the differentiation — the variety — of the objects (<s>grāhya</s>) and subjects (<s>grāhaka</s>) that are mutually adapted — i.e., that stand in mutual fitness with one another. Thus, at the level of the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-principle, the universe as object — in which 'this-ness' (<s>idantā</s>) is indistinct, covered by 'I-ness' (<s>ahantā</s>), of a supreme-and-higher nature — is just such [as the subject]; and the class of knowers called <s>Mantra-Maheśvaras</s>, presided over by the Lord <s>Sadāśiva</s>, are established in just such a condition by the will of the Supreme Lord. At the <s>Īśvara</s>-principle, where the universe as object has the nature of the co-referentiality of distinct 'this-ness' and 'I-ness' — just such is the class of <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, presided over by the Lord <s>Īśvara</s>. At the stage of <s>Vidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), the <s>Mantras</s> — as knowers, presided over by the venerable Lord <s>Ananta</s>, divided into many branches and sub-divisions, existing as they truly are — have as their object a universe whose essence is differentiation alone, of the same nature. Above <s>Māyā</s>, the <s>Vijñānākalas</s> — whose nature is pure consciousness devoid of agency — have as their object [a reality] whose essence is non-difference from them, familiar through the previous states of <s>Sakala</s>, <s>Pralaya</s>, and <s>Akala</s>. In <s>Māyā</s>, the void-knowers (<s>śūnya-pramātṛ</s>), the <s>Pralayakevalins</s>, have as their object what is fitting for them — [a reality] as if dissolved. For the <s>Sakalas</s>, who are situated [in the levels] down to the earth — who are limited and completely differentiated — their object is of just such a nature. For the Lord <s>Śiva</s> who transcends these, whose sole body is luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), the entities are of the sole form of luminosity. For the blessed Supreme <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Paramaśiva</s>) — who transcends the universe yet is the Self of the universe, a single mass of luminosity pervaded by supreme bliss — the entire [reality] from <s>Śiva</s> down to the earth flashes forth in non-difference alone. In truth, there is no object (<s>grāhya</s>) or subject (<s>grāhaka</s>) that is other [than Him]. Rather, it is the Lord Supreme <s>Śiva</s> alone who flashes forth thus, with thousands of manifold varieties — this is essentially what has been stated. ||

children.text: yathā ca bhagavān viśvaśarīraḥ tathā
children.translated_text: And just as the Lord has the universe as His body, so too:

children.text: citisaṃkocātmā cetano 'pi saṃkucitaviśvamayaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Even the individual conscious being (<s>cetana</s>), [who is but] consciousness in a contracted state, contains the universe in a contracted form. || Sūtra 4 ||

children.text:
śrīparamaśivaḥ svātmaikyena sthitaṃ viśvaṃ sadāśivādyucitena rūpena
avabibhāsayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ
cidaikyākhyātimayānāśritaśivaparyāyaśūnyātiśūnyātmatayā prakāśābhedena
prakāśamānatayā sphurati | tataḥ
cidrasāśyānatārūpāśeṣatattvabhuvanabhāvatattatpramātrādyātmatayāpi
prathate | yathā ca evaṃ bhagavān viśvaśarīraḥ tathā citisaṃkocātmā
saṃkucitacidrūpaḥ cetano grāhako 'pi vaṭadhānikāvat
saṃkucitāśeṣaviśvarūpaḥ | tathā ca siddhāntavacanam
children.translated_text: The blessed Supreme <s>Śiva</s>, wishing to manifest the universe — which abides in identity with His own Self — in the form appropriate [to each level] from <s>Sadāśiva</s> onward, first flashes forth in non-difference from luminosity, in the mode of the Void-beyond-Void (<s>śūnyātiśūnya</s>) — synonymous with <s>Śiva</s> in the unmanifest state, whose nature is the unbroken unity of Consciousness-as-Identity (<s>cidaikyākhyāti</s>). Then He also manifests as the Self of each and every principle, world, entity, knower, etc. — [all of] which are [really] the relaxation of the savor of consciousness (<s>cit-rasa</s>). And just as the Lord thus has the universe as His body, so too the individual conscious being (<s>cetana</s>) — the knowing subject — though [merely] consciousness in a contracted state (<s>citi-saṃkoca</s>), is of the nature of the entire universe in a contracted form, like a banyan seed. And thus the statement of the <s>Siddhānta</s> [tradition]:

children.text: vigraho vigrahī caiva sarvavigrahavigrahī | iti |
children.translated_text: '[He is] the body and the embodied one, and the embodied one of all bodies.' //

children.text: triśiromate 'pi=20
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Triśiromata</s> [tantra] also:

children.text: sarvadevamayaḥ kāyas taṃ cedānīṃ śṛṇu priye |
children.translated_text: 'The body is composed of all the gods — now hear about that, O dear one!

children.text: pṛthivī kaṭhinatvena dravatve 'mbhaḥ prakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Earth [is present] in [the quality of] hardness; water is declared [to be present] in fluidity.' //

children.text: ity upakramya=20
children.translated_text: Beginning thus, and ending with:

children.text: triśirobhairavaḥ sākṣād vyāpya viśvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Triśirobhairava</s> himself, pervading the universe, abides [in the body].' //

children.text:
ity antena granthena grāhakasya saṃkucitaviśvamayatvam eva vyāharati |
ayaṃ cātrāśayaḥ grāhako 'pi ayaṃ prakāśaikātmyena uktāgamayuktyā ca
viśvaśarīraśivaikarūpa eva kevalaṃ tanmāyāśaktyā
anabhivyaktasvarūpatvāt saṃkucita iva ābhāti | saṃkoco 'pi vicāryamāṇaḥ
cidaikātmyena prathamānatvāt cinmaya eva | anyathā tu na kiṃcit iti sarvo
grāhako viśvaśarīraḥ śivabhaṭṭāraka eva | tad uktaṃ mayaiva
children.translated_text: — by this entire passage, the very fact that the individual knowing subject contains the universe in a contracted form is declared. And the intended meaning here is this: this knowing subject too, by the logic and scripture already stated, is of the sole form of <s>Śiva</s> who has the universe as His body, in identity with luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>); it is merely that, due to His <s>Māyā-śakti</s>, his own essential nature is not manifested, and so he appears as if contracted. Even the contraction, when examined, since it manifests in identity with consciousness, is itself of the nature of consciousness. Otherwise, it would be nothing at all. Therefore, every knowing subject is the Lord <s>Śiva</s> Himself, who has the universe as His body. As I myself have said:

children.text:
akhyātir yadi na khyāti khyātir evāvaśiṣyate |
khyāti cet khyātirūpatvāt khyātir evāvaśiṣyate || iti |
children.translated_text: 'If non-cognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) does not shine, then cognition (<s>khyāti</s>) alone remains. If [non-cognition] does shine, then, being of the nature of cognition, cognition alone remains.' //

children.text: anenaivāśayena śrīspandaśāstreṣu
children.translated_text: With this very intention, in the venerable <s>Spanda-śāstras</s>:

children.text: yasmāt sarvamayo jīvaḥ ............................ |
children.translated_text: 'Since the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) is identical with everything...' //

children.text: ity upakramya=20
children.translated_text: — beginning thus, and [ending with]:

children.text: tena śabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yaḥ śivaḥ [4] |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore there is no state in the contemplation of words and their meanings that is not <s>Śiva</s>.' //

children.text:
ityādinā śivajīvayor abheda evoktaḥ | etattattvaparijñānam eva muktiḥ |
etattattvāparijñānam eva ca bandha iti bhaviṣyati eva etat ||
children.translated_text: — by such [statements], the non-difference of <s>Śiva</s> and the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) alone is declared. The complete knowledge of this truth is itself liberation (<s>mukti</s>); and the non-knowledge of this truth is itself bondage (<s>bandha</s>) — this will indeed be [demonstrated later]. ||

children.text:
nanu grāhako 'yaṃ vikalpamayaḥ vikalpanaṃ ca cittahetukaṃ sati ca citte
katham asya śivātmakatvaṃ iti śaṅktvā cittam eva nirnetum āha
children.translated_text: Now, [one might object:] 'This perceiver is constituted by thought-constructs (<s>vikalpa</s>), and thought-construction is caused by the mind (<s>citta</s>); and if the mind exists, how can it have the nature of <s>Śiva</s>?' Anticipating this doubt, he speaks in order to analyze the mind itself:

children.text: citir eva cetanapadād avarūḍhā cetyasaṃkocinī
cittam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: is the mind (<s>citta</s>). || 5 ||
Consciousness (<s>citi</s>) itself, descended from the stage of the conscious (<s>cetana</s>), contracting in the form of the knowable (<s>cetya</s>),

children.text:
na cittaṃ nāma anyat kiṃcit api tu saiva bhagavatī tat | tathā hi sā sva.=

ullasitam api saṃkocaṃ guṇīkṛtya citprādhānyena sphurati | kadācit

The mind is not something other [than consciousness]; rather, it is that very divine [consciousness] (<s>bhagavatī</s>). For when she, concealing her own essential nature, assumes contraction, there are two possibilities: sometimes, although contraction has arisen, she makes it subordinate and shines forth with consciousness (<s>cit</s>) as predominant; sometimes, with contraction as predominant. In the case where consciousness predominates: when pure luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) alone is predominant in its natural [state], there is the state of <s>vijñānākala</s> (the bodiless knower). When luminosity along with reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>) predominates, there is the status of the <s>vidyā</s>-subject (the knowing experiencer). And therein, as contraction progressively diminishes, there is the form of <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and the un-attributed. But when the predominance of consciousness is acquired through the effort of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), there is the status of the subject of the pure path (<s>śuddhādhva</s>), progressively more excellent. When contraction predominates, however, there is the status of the void-subject (<s>śūnyapramātṛ</s>) etc. This being the case, consciousness (<s>citi</s>) itself, in its contracted form as the perceiver, having descended from the stage of the conscious, becoming oriented toward the grasping of objects, contracting through the knowable (<s>cetya</s>) such as blue, pleasure, etc., contracted by the double contraction [of subject and object], is

Thus it is stated in the <s>Śrī Pratyabhijñā</s>. Therefore, in the <s>Śrī Tattvagarbhastotra</s>, with the intention of following that [true nature], since the real essential nature exists even in the state of thought-construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), it is said —

children.translated_text: The level of body and <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is indeed predominantly [governed by] the mind. Even the void-plane (<s>śūnyabhūmi</s>) possesses the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of the mind. Otherwise, for one who has emerged from that [state], there would be no pursuit of his own duties — therefore the <s>māyīya</s> (māyā-based) experiencer is indeed constituted of the mind. With this very intention, in the <s>Śivasūtras</s>, following the actual state of affairs, having stated '<s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness) is the Self' [1.1], then, at the occasion of defining the <s>māyā</s>-experiencer, it is said again: 'The mind (<s>citta</s>) is the Self' [3.1].

children.translated_text: From the perspective that has been established, the Self, whose essence is consciousness (<s>cidātmā</s>), is the revered <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Śivabhaṭṭāraka</s>) alone — one, and not anyone else, since luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) cannot be divided by space, time, etc. And the inert (<s>jaḍa</s>) cannot serve as a perceiver. Since it is luminosity itself that, through [its] absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), having assumed the contraction of <s>prāṇa</s> etc., attains the state of a contracted perceiver of objects — therefore he is of two forms, by virtue of [both] having the nature of luminosity and having the appearance of contraction. He is threefold, because of being covered by the three impurities (<s>malas</s>): <s>āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual), <s>māyīya</s> (pertaining to <s>māyā</s>), and <s>kārmika</s> (pertaining to <s>karma</s>). He is fourfold, because of having the nature of the void (<s>śūnya</s>), <s>prāṇa</s>, the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), and the [gross] body (<s>śarīra</s>). The seven pentads are the thirty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>Śiva</s> to <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) — he is of that nature. Likewise, he has the nature of the seven [levels of] experiencers from <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>Sakala</s>. And though having the form of the five powers — consciousness (<s>cit</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>) — due to the force of non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>), because of being encased in the five coverings (<s>kañcukas</s>) of <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Rāga</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and <s>Niyati</s>, he has the nature of [those] five. And thus, being recognized as having the single form of <s>Śiva</s>, as being constituted of the thirty-five <s>tattvas</s>, as having the nature of the seven [levels of] experiencers, and as being of the essence of the five powers beginning with <s>cit</s> — this is liberation (<s>mukti</s>). Otherwise, it is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.translated_text: The established doctrines (<s>siddhāntas</s>) of all philosophical systems — <s>Cārvāka</s> and others — are the stages of this Self, assumed by his own will like [the roles of] an actor, and hence artificial. Namely: the <s>Cārvākas</s> [hold that] the Self is the body endowed with consciousness. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others consider the Self in <s>saṃsāra</s> as essentially the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect-principle), the substratum of qualities such as knowledge; but in liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), with the cessation of that, [the Self becomes] essentially void. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> too, considering the Self to be the object of the 'I'-cognition, obscured by conditions (<s>upādhis</s>) of pleasure, pain, etc., are really established in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) alone. The <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists), [holding that] the continuum of cognitions alone is the reality, end up in the modifications of the intellect alone. Some Vedāntins [hold that] '<s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the Self.' The proponents of the void-<s>Brahman</s>, [citing] 'This was indeed non-existent,' are immersed in the void-plane. The <s>Mādhyamikas</s> likewise. The <s>Pāñcarātras</s>, [holding that] the supreme <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) is the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> and that individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>) are merely his sparks — because they accept the transformation of the supreme <s>Prakṛti</s> — are really established in the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others rest on the plane of the <s>vijñānākala</s> (bodiless knower). Other Vedāntins, [citing] 'This was indeed existent in the beginning,' have taken refuge in the level of the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>. The Grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>), [holding that] the Self-<s>tattva</s> has the form of <s>Paśyantī</s> (the Seeing [level of speech]) and is constituted of <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (the Word-Absolute), are established in the level of <s>Śrī Sadāśiva</s>. Other [systems] too should be understood similarly. And this is set forth in the <s>Āgamas</s> —

children.translated_text: The <s>Tāntrikas</s> [hold that] the Self-<s>tattva</s> transcends the universe; those established in the <s>Kula</s> and other traditions [hold it to be] identical with the universe; and those who know the <s>Trika</s> and other systems [hold it to be] both transcending and constituting the universe. Thus, all these stages are manifested by the absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) of the one Lord whose essence is consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>), differentiated by varying degrees of concealment and revelation of [that] freedom. Therefore, the Self alone has this extent of pervasion. But those of limited vision, by his will alone, are made to identify with partial and fragmentary [stages], whereby, even though the essence of the pervasion of prior experiencers is spread out in stages such as the body etc., they do not attain the great pervasion (<s>mahāvyāpti</s>) of the nature described, without the descent of supreme power (<s>paraśaktipāta</s>). As it is said —

children.translated_text: Moreover, the 'resting states' (<s>sthiti</s>) — the inward-facing repose — of all philosophical systems, and of all cognitions such as blue, pleasure, etc., are 'stages of that' [Self], [i.e.,] means for the manifestation of one's own essential nature, which is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>). For whenever the outward-facing form comes to rest in [its] essential nature, then there occurs the withdrawal of external objects, the abiding in the inner state of peace, and the threading together of the succession of cognitions about to arise. Thus this <s>Turīyā</s> (the Fourth), the sovereign Consciousness (<s>saṃvidbhaṭṭārikā</s>), in the form of the fusion of creation, maintenance, and dissolution — emitting and withdrawing the varieties of creation etc. — is always full yet diminished, of both forms yet of neither form, shining forth non-sequentially. And it is said in the <s>Śrī Pratyabhijñā-ṭīkā</s> (commentary on the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>) —

children.translated_text: When the Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), whose nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>), by His own absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), submerges the non-differentiated pervasion (<s>abhedavyāpti</s>) and takes hold of the differentiated pervasion (<s>bhedavyāpti</s>), then His powers of will (<s>icchā</s>) and the rest, though [in reality] uncontracted, appear as if contracted. At that very time, He becomes a bound soul (<s>saṃsārin</s>), covered by impurity (<s>mala</s>). Thus: the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>), whose form is unobstructed freedom, when contracted, [becomes] the <s>āṇava mala</s> (innate impurity) in the form of a sense of incompleteness. The power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), through gradual contraction, [arrives at] the attainment of limited knowledge (<s>kiṃcijjñatva</s>) in place of omniscience in [the realm of] differentiation — and through the assumption of extreme contraction in the form of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) and the cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), [becomes] the <s>māyīya mala</s> (impurity of māyā), whose nature is the manifestation of differentiated objects. The power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>), through gradual [contraction], in the attainment of limited agency (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>) in place of omnipotence in differentiation — and through the assumption of the contraction in the form of the organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>), having arrived at extreme limitation, [becomes] the <s>kārma mala</s> (impurity of action), consisting of meritorious and demeritorious deeds. Likewise, the powers of omnipotence, omniscience, completeness, eternity, and all-pervasiveness, when assuming contraction, appear respectively as <s>kalā</s> (limited agency), <s>vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>niyati</s> (spatial limitation). And one of this kind, impoverished in powers, is called a bound soul (<s>saṃsārin</s>). But in the unfoldment of his own powers, he is <s>Śiva</s> Himself.

children.text:
nanu saṃsāryavasthāyām asya kiṃcit śivatocitaṃ abhijñānam asti yena
śiva eva tathāvasthita ity udghoṣyate astītyāha
children.translated_text: But even in the state of being a bound soul, does he possess some awareness befitting <s>Śiva</s>, by which it may be proclaimed that [he is] <s>Śiva</s> Himself, though in such a condition? Yes, he says —

children.text: tathāpi tadvat pañcakṛtyāni karoti || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Even so, He performs the five acts (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) in that very manner. || 10 ||

children.text:
iha īśvarādvayadarśanasya brahmavādibhyaḥ ayam eva viśeṣaḥ |
yat=20
children.translated_text: Here, this is the very distinction of the doctrine of non-dual <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) from the <s>Brahmavādins</s> (Vedāntins): namely,

children.text: sṛṣṭisaṃhārakartāraṃ vilayasthitikārakam |
children.translated_text: [He is] the performer of creation and dissolution, the one who brings about withdrawal and maintenance,

children.text: anugrahakaraṃ devaṃ praṇatārtivināśanam [13] || iti
children.translated_text: the bestower of grace (<s>anugraha</s>), the God who destroys the suffering of those who bow down.

children.text:
śrimatsvacchandādiśāsanoktanītyā sadā pañcavidhakṛtyakāritvaṃ cidātmano
bhagavataḥ | yathā ca bhagavān śuddhetarādhvasphāraṇakrameṇa
svarūpavikāsarūpāṇi sṛṣṭyādīni karoti tathā saṃkucitacicchaktyā

children.translated_text: In accordance with the method taught in the revered <s>Svacchanda</s> and other scriptures, the <s>Bhagavān</s> whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>) always performs the five acts. And just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> performs creation and the rest — which are in the nature of the unfoldment of His own essential nature — through the process of manifesting the pure and impure paths (<s>adhvan</s>), so too, with His contracted power of consciousness, He performs the five acts even on the plane of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). For thus —

children.text: tad evaṃ vyavahāre 'pi prabhur dehādim āviśan |
children.translated_text: Even in worldly activity, the Lord, entering the body and the rest,

children.text: bhāntam evāntararthaugham icchayā bhāsayed bahiḥ [14] ||
children.translated_text: manifests outwardly, by [His] will (<s>icchā</s>), the mass of inner objects that shines [within].

children.translated_text: In accordance with the meaning stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā Kārikās</s> — the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), whose nature is consciousness, entering the plane of body, vital breath, and the rest, at the occasion of outward-facing [awareness], when He manifests an object such as blue with the appearance of fixed place, time, and so on — then, with respect to the aspect of appearance of fixed place and time, He has the role of creator (<s>sraṣṭṛ</s>). With respect to the aspect of appearance of other places and times, He has the role of dissolver (<s>saṃhartṛ</s>). With respect to the aspect of appearance of blue and the like, [He has] the role of maintainer (<s>sthāpaka</s>). With respect to the aspect of appearance as differentiated, [He has] the role of causing withdrawal (<s>vilayakārin</s>). In the illumination through the unity of light (<s>prakāśa</s>), [He has] the role of bestower of grace (<s>anugrahītṛ</s>). And just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> always performs the five acts, so has been thoroughly demonstrated by me in the <s>Spandasandoha</s>. Thus, this fivefold act-performance, when recognized as one's own through firm conviction and constantly contemplated, unfolds divine sovereignty (<s>māheśvarya</s>) for those who possess devotion (<s>bhakti</s>). Therefore, those who constantly contemplate this, knowing the universe as consisting of the unfoldment of their own essential nature, are proclaimed as 'liberated while living' (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). But those who do not [contemplate thus], seeing the entirety of knowable objects as completely separate [from themselves], are bound souls.

children.text:

children.translated_text: And this is not the only mode of the performance of the five acts — there is yet another, of a secret nature, he says —

Through manifestation (<s>ābhāsana</s>), relishing (<s>rakti</s>), reflective awareness (<s>vimarśana</s>), seeding (<s>bījāvasthāpana</s>), and dissolution (<s>vilāpana</s>) —

children.text:
pañcavidhakṛtyāni karoti iti pūrvataḥ saṃbadhyate |

children.translated_text: 'He performs the five acts' is to be connected from the previous [sūtra]. According to the revered <s>Mahārtha</s> (Great Meaning) perspective, whatever appears through the process of the extension of the goddesses (<s>devī</s>) beginning with sight (<s>dṛk</s>) — that is 'created' (<s>sṛjyate</s>). Then, when [consciousness] is 'colored' (<s>rajyati</s>) by that which has been thus created — i.e., when for some time it rests there with closed eyelids (without blinking), as it were — then it is 'maintained' by the goddess of maintenance (<s>sthitidevī</s>). But at the moment of 'reflective awareness' (<s>vimarśana</s>) — which is another name for wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — it is 'dissolved.' As stated by the revered <s>Rāma</s>:

samādhivajreṇāpy anyair abhedyo bhedabhūdharaḥ |
parāmṛṣṭaś ca naṣṭaś ca tvadbhaktibalaśālibhiḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The mountain of differentiation, unbreakable even by the thunderbolt of <s>samādhi</s> by others, is grasped and destroyed by those who possess the strength of devotion to You.' ||

And such

children.translated_text: In the non-recognition of this always-occurring fivefold act-performance — [i.e.,] in the absence of its becoming manifest due to the lack of the unfoldment of one's own power caused by the descent of <s>Śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>) — delusion by one's own powers means being transfixed by the stake of various mundane and scriptural doubts — this itself is the state of being a bound soul (<s>saṃsāritva</s>). As stated in the revered <s>Sarvavīrabhaṭṭāraka</s>:

children.translated_text: For indeed, this supreme speech-power (<s>parāvākśakti</s>) — inseparable from the light of consciousness (<s>citprakāśa</s>), of the nature of the eternally-arisen great <s>mantra</s>, consisting of the full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃvimarśa</s>), pregnant with the entire circle of powers in the form [of the alphabet] from 'a' to 'kṣa' — first, through the sequence of <s>Paśyantī</s> (visionary) and <s>Madhyamā</s> (intermediate [speech]), illuminates the plane of the subject (<s>grāhaka</s>). And there, not manifesting her own essential nature as being of the form of <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme), she unfolds for the subject of <s>Māyā</s> a conceptual activity (<s>vikalpakriyā</s>) that is ever-new at every moment, in the form of indistinct and non-shared object-appearance. And she displays even the pure, non-conceptual ground (<s>avikalpabhūmi</s>) as veiled by that [conceptual activity]. And therein, the deluded person (<s>mūḍhajana</s>), bewildered by the diverse powers of the letters 'ka' etc., presided over by the goddesses <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest, considers the self as merely the limited body, vital breath, and the rest. The goddesses <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest, in the condition of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), manifesting creation and maintenance in the domain of differentiation and dissolution in the domain of non-differentiation, bring about only the receptivity for limited conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). But in the condition of a master (<s>pati</s>), manifesting dissolution in differentiation and creation-maintenance in non-differentiation, they gradually, through the progressive diminution of <s>vikalpa</s>, unfold the great non-conceptual ground (<s>avikalpabhūmi</s>) that consists of entry into the revered seal of <s>Bhairava</s> (<s>Bhairavamudrā</s>).

children.text: sarvo mamāyaṃ vibhava ity evaṃ parijānataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'All this glory is mine' — for one who knows thus,

children.translated_text: They unfold the pure <s>vikalpa</s>-power — of the form just described, immersed in the absorption of consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>). Therefore, in the manner stated, it is delusion by one's own powers alone that constitutes the state of bondage. Moreover, the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) itself — the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (divine goddess) — because of emitting the universe and because of the 'left-hand' conduct of <s>saṃsāra</s> (<s>saṃsāravāmācāratva</s>), being called <s>Vāmeśvarī</s> (the Left-hand Goddess), scintillating through all [forms as] the subjects (<s>pramātṛ</s>), inner organs (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), outer organs (<s>bahiṣkaraṇa</s>), and objects (<s>bhāva</s>) — in the plane of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), resting in the void (<s>śūnyapada</s>), shines forth through the <s>Khecarī</s> circle (in the form of limited agency and the powers of <s>kalā</s> and the rest) with its true nature of consciousness-space-wandering concealed. Through the <s>Gocarī</s> circle (in the form of inner organ-goddesses dominated by the conceptualization of affirmation of difference) she shines with her true ultimate nature of affirmation of non-difference concealed. Through the <s>Dikcarī</s> circle (in the form of outer organ-deities dominated by the perception of difference and the like) she manifests with her true ultimate nature of the display of non-difference concealed. And through the <s>Bhūcarī</s> circle (in the nature of cognized objects whose appearance is completely delimited), she shines with her true nature of universal identity concealed — deluding the heart of the bound soul. But on the plane of the master (<s>pati</s>), she manifests through <s>Khecarī</s>-ness as consciousness-space-wandering of the nature of all powers including omnipotence; through <s>Gocarī</s>-ness as the nature of affirmation of non-difference; through <s>Dikcarī</s>-ness as the nature of perception of non-difference; and through <s>Bhūcarī</s>-ness as cognized objects whose essence is the display of non-duality as one's own limbs — blossoming the heart of the master. And thus it was stated by <s>Bhaṭṭa Dāmodara</s>, with spontaneous wonder generating unaffected reverence, in the <s>Vimuktaka</s>:

children.translated_text: And thus, the state of being a transmigrating soul (<s>saṃsāritva</s>) consists precisely in being deluded by one's own power (<s>śakti</s>). Moreover, the Supreme Lord, whose nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>), has His own inseparable, single power of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya-śakti</s>), whose essence is the agency (<s>kartṛtā</s>) that is the core of the flash of awareness (<s>sphurattā</s>). When that [power], concealing its own essential nature, deludes [the individual] at the level of the bound soul (<s>pāśava-pada</s>) through the states of the powers of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s>, through the stages of waking, dream, and deep sleep, and through the <s>kalās</s> (phases) of body, vital breath, and the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) — then the state of being deluded by that [power] is the state of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>). But when She unfolds the <s>udāna-śakti</s> (power of ascent), which is the flourishing of the central channel (<s>madhya-dhāman</s>), and the <s>vyāna-śakti</s> (power of pervasion), whose essence is the pervading of the universe — [the former] having the form of the <s>turya</s> (fourth state) and [the latter] the form of the state beyond the fourth (<s>turyātīta</s>), both being a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>) — then, even in the condition of the body etc., one becomes a living liberated being (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), having the nature of the Lord's state. Thus the threefold delusion by one's own power has been explained. In the sūtra '<s>cidvat</s>...' [Sūtra 5], it was said: 'The light of consciousness, having assumed contraction, is the transmigrating soul.' But here it is said by a different turn of phrase that this one's state of transmigration is due to being deluded by one's own power. Thus, when the one whose powers are contracted, even while possessing the vital breath etc., is not deluded by his own power, then by the scriptural declaration — 'this embodied one is the Supreme Lord' — it is indirectly established that he is none other than the Lord <s>Śiva</s>. As the <s>Āgama</s> [states]:

children.text: manuṣyadeham āsthāya channās te parameśvarāḥ | iti |
children.translated_text: 'Having assumed a human body, these Supreme Lords abide in concealment.' //

children.text:
uktam ca pratyabhijñāṭīkāyāṃ "śarīram eva ghaṭādy api vā ye
ṣaṭtriṃśattattvamayaṃ śivarūpatayāpaśyanti te 'pi sidhyanti" iti ||
children.translated_text: And it is stated in the commentary on the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>: 'Those who see even the body itself — or even a pot etc. — which consists of the thirty-six principles, as being of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> — they too attain <s>siddhi</s> (perfection).' ||

children.text: uktasūtrārthaprātipakṣyeṇa tattvadṛṣṭiṃ darśayitum āha
children.translated_text: In order to show the vision of truth (<s>tattva-dṛṣṭi</s>) as the counterpart of the meaning of the [previously] stated sūtras, he says:

children.text: tatparijñāne cittam eva antarmukhībhāvena
cetanapadādhyārohāt citiḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: by ascending to the stage of the conscious subject (<s>cetana-pada</s>), [becomes] <s>Citi</s> (universal Consciousness). || Sūtra 13 ||
For the complete knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of that, the <s>citta</s> (individual mind) itself, through turning inward (<s>antarmukhībhāva</s>),

children.text:
pūrvasūtravyākhyāprasaṅgena prameyadṛṣṭyā vitatya vyākhyātaprāyam etat
sūtram | śabdasaṃgatyā tu adhunā vyākhyāyate | tasyātmīyasya
pañcakṛtyakāritvasya parijñāne sati aparijñānalakṣaṇakāraṇāpagamāt
svaśaktivyāmohitatānivṛttau svātantryalabhāt prāk vyākhyātaṃ yat cittaṃ
tad eva saṃkocinīṃ bahirmukhatāṃ jahat antarmukhībhāvena
cetanapadādhyārohāt grāhakabhūmikākramaṇakrameṇa saṃkocakalāyā api
vigalanena svarūpāpattyā citir bhavati | svāṃ cinmayīṃ parāṃ bhūmim
āviśatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This sūtra has been mostly explained at length from the perspective of the object (<s>prameya</s>), in connection with the commentary on the previous sūtras. But now it is explained from the perspective of verbal construction. When there is complete knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of that — one's own authorship of the five acts (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) — since the cause, which is the non-knowledge [thereof], is removed, and since the delusion by one's own power ceases and autonomy is regained — [then] the <s>citta</s> (individual mind), previously explained, abandoning the contracting outward-facing orientation, through turning inward (<s>antarmukhībhāva</s>), by ascending to the stage of the conscious subject (<s>cetana-pada</s>) — i.e., by progressively entering the levels of the knower (<s>grāhaka</s>) — with the melting away even of the phase of contraction (<s>saṃkoca-kalā</s>), through the recovery of its own essential nature, becomes <s>Citi</s> (universal Consciousness). The meaning is: it enters its own ground of consciousness (<s>cinmayī parā bhūmi</s>). ||

children.text:
nanu yadi pāramārthikaṃ cicchaktipadaṃ sakalabhedakavalanasvabhāvaṃ [17]
tad asya māyāpade 'pi tathārūpeṇa bhavitavyaṃ yathā jaladācchāditasyāpi
bhānoḥ bhāvāvabhāsakatvaṃ ity āśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Objection: If the ultimate stage of the power of consciousness, whose nature is the swallowing of all differentiation, is [always real], then even at the level of <s>Māyā</s>, it should exist in that very form — just as the sun, even when covered by clouds, retains its capacity to illuminate objects. Anticipating this, he says:

children.text: citivahnir arohapade channo 'pi mātrayā
meyendhanaṃ pluṣyati || 14 ||
children.translated_text: burns the fuel of the objects of knowledge (<s>meya-indhana</s>). || Sūtra 14 ||
The fire of consciousness (<s>citi-vahni</s>), even when concealed at the stage of descent, by [its] portion (<s>mātrā</s>),

children.text:
citir eva viśvagrasanaśīlatvāt vahniḥ | asau eva avarohapade
māyāpramātṛtāyāṃ channo 'pi svātantryāt ācchāditasvabhāvo 'pi
bhūribhūtichannāgnivat mātrayā aṃśena nīlapītādiprameyendhanaṃ pluṣyati
svātmasātkaroti | mātrāpadasyedam ākūtaṃ yat kavalayann api sārvātmyena na
grasate api tu aṃśena saṃskārātmanā utthāpayati |
grāsakatvaṃ ca sarvapramātṝṇāṃ svānubhavata eva siddham | yad uktaṃ
śrīmadutpaladevapādaiḥ nijastotreṣu
children.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>citi</s>) itself, due to its nature of devouring the universe, is called fire (<s>vahni</s>). That very [fire], at the stage of descent — i.e., at the level of the <s>Māyā</s>-knower — even when concealed, i.e., even when its essential nature is covered — like a fire hidden beneath a great heap of ashes — by [its] portion (<s>mātrā</s>), i.e., partially, burns the fuel of objects such as blue, yellow, etc. — i.e., assimilates them into its own Self. The intended meaning of the word <s>mātrā</s> (portion) is this: although it does devour [the objects], it does not consume them in their totality; rather, it raises them up partially, in the form of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>). And the devouring capacity is established for all knowers from their own experience. As stated by the venerable <s>Utpaladeva</s> in his own hymns:

children.text: vartante jantavo 'śeṣā api brahmendraviṣṇavaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'All beings, including <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, subsist

children.text: grasamānās tato vande deva viśvaṃ bhavanmayam [18] || iti ||
children.translated_text: while devouring [the universe]; therefore I worship You, O God — the universe is pervaded by You.' ||

children.text:
yadā punaḥ karaṇeśvarīprasarasaṃkocaṃ saṃpādya
sargasaṃhārakramapariśīlanayuktiṃ āviśati tadā
children.translated_text: But when, having accomplished the expansion and contraction of the ruling powers of the faculties (<s>karaṇeśvarī</s>), one enters the method of practicing the process of creation and dissolution — then:

children.text: balalābhe viśvam ātmasātkaroti || 15 ||
children.translated_text: Upon the attainment of power (<s>bala-lābha</s>), [the yogin] assimilates the universe into the Self. || Sūtra 15 ||

children.text:
citir eva dehaprāṇādyācchādananimajjanena svarūpaṃ unmagnatvena
sphārayantī balam | yathoktam
children.translated_text: It is consciousness (<s>citi</s>) itself that, by submerging beneath the coverings of body, vital breath, etc., and then causing its own essential nature to expand by [the process of] emergence — [this is called] power (<s>bala</s>). As stated:

children.text: tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ ... ... [19] | iti |
children.translated_text: 'Having mounted upon that power, the <s>mantras</s>...' //

children.text:
evaṃ ca balalābhe unmagnasvarūpāśrayaṇe kṣityādisadāśivāntaṃ viśvaṃ
ātmasātkaroti svasvarūpābhedena nirbhāsayati |
tad uktaṃ pūrvagurubhiḥ svabhāṣāmayeṣu kramasūtreṣu
children.translated_text: And thus, upon the attainment of power — the resort to [one's] emerged essential nature — one assimilates the universe from earth up to <s>Sadāśiva</s> into the Self, i.e., causes it to shine forth in non-difference from one's own essential nature. As stated by the earlier teachers in the <s>Krama-sūtras</s> composed in the vernacular language:

children.text:
yathā vahnir udbodhito dāhyaṃ dahati tathā viṣayapāśān bhakṣayet | iti =
|
children.translated_text: 'Just as fire, when kindled, burns the fuel — so should one consume the bonds of sense-objects.' //

children.text:
na caivaṃ vaktavyam =AD viśvātmasātkārarūpā samāveśabhūḥ kādācitkī |
kathaṃ upādeyā iyaṃ syād iti yato dehādyunmajjananimajjanavaśena iyaṃ
asyāḥ kādācitkatvam iva ābhāti | vastutas tu
citisvātantryāvabhāsitadehādyunmajjanād eva kādācitkatvam |
eṣā tu sadaiva prakāśamānā | anyathā tad dehādy api na prakāśeta |
ata eva dehādipramātṛtābhimānanimajjanāya abhyāsaḥ | na tu
sadāprathamānatāsārapramātṛtāprāptyarthaṃ iti śrīpratyabhijñākārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And one should not say: 'The state of <s>samāveśa</s> (immersion), whose nature is the assimilation of the universe into the Self, is occasional; how can it be something to be pursued?' — for it merely appears to be occasional due to the emergence and submergence of body etc. In reality, the apparent occasionality is due to the emergence of body etc. being manifested by the autonomy of consciousness. But this [consciousness] shines always. Otherwise, even the body etc. would not shine [at all]. Therefore, the practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) is for the submergence of the identification with the body etc. as a knower — not for the attainment of the state of the knower whose essence is ever-primary manifestation. Thus [say] the authors of the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>. ||

children.text: evaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And thus:

children.text: cidānandalābhe dehādiṣu cetyamāneṣv api
cidaikātmyapratipattidārḍhyaṃ jīvanmuktiḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the firmness of the realization of identity with consciousness alone is living liberation (<s>jīvanmukti</s>). || Sūtra 16 ||
Upon the attainment of the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda</s>), even when body and the like are perceived as objects (<s>cetya</s>),

children.text:
viśvātmasātkārātmani samāveśarūpe cidānande labdhe vyutthānadaśāyāṃ
dalakalpatayā dehaprāṇanīlasukhādiṣu ābhāsamāneṣv api yat
samāveśasaṃskārabalāt pratipādayiṣyamāṇayuktikramopabṛṃhitāt
cidaikātmyapratipattidārḍhyam |
avicalā cidekatvaprathā saiva jīvanmuktiḥ jīvataḥ prāṇān api dhārayato
muktiḥ pratyabhijñātanijasvarūpavidrāvitāśeṣapāśarāśitvāt |
children.translated_text: When the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda</s>), whose nature is the <s>samāveśa</s> (immersion) consisting of the assimilation of the universe into the Self, has been attained, [then] in the state of emergence from [meditation] (<s>vyutthāna</s>), even when body, vital breath, blue, pleasure, etc. appear as mere leaves [i.e., insubstantial appearances] — the firmness of the realization of identity with consciousness alone, [arising] from the force of the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of [previous] <s>samāveśa</s>, strengthened by the progressive method of reasoning to be explained — the unwavering expansion of the unity of consciousness — that itself is living liberation (<s>jīvanmukti</s>): liberation while still alive, while still sustaining the vital breaths, because the entire mass of bonds has been dissolved through the recognition of one's own essential nature.

children.text: yathoktaṃ spandaśāstre
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Spandaśāstra</s>:

children.text: iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ krīḍātvenākhilaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: 'Or, he whose awareness [is such that] the entire universe is [his] play —

children.text: sa paśyan satataṃ yukto jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ [20] || iti ||
children.translated_text: he, seeing [thus] constantly, is united (<s>yukta</s>); he is a living liberated being — there is no doubt.' ||

children.text: atha kathaṃ cidānandalābho bhavati ity āha
children.translated_text: Now, how does the attainment of the bliss of consciousness come about? He says:

children.text: madhyavikāsāc cidānandalābhaḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: Through the expansion of the center (<s>madhya-vikāsa</s>), [there is] the attainment of the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda-lābha</s>). || Sūtra 17 ||

children.text:
sarvāntaratamatvena vartamānatvāt tadbhittilagnatāṃ vinā ca kasyacid api
svarūpānupapatteḥ saṃvid eva bhagavatī madhyam | sā tu māyādaśāyāṃ
tathābhūtāpi svarūpaṃ gūhayitvā "prāk saṃvit prāṇe pariṇatā " iti nītyā
prāṇaśaktibhūmiṃ svīkṛtya avarohakrameṇa buddhidehādibhuvaṃ
adhiśayānā nāḍīsahasrasaraṇim anusṛtā |
tatrāpi ca palāśaparṇamadhyaśākhānyāyena ābrahmarandhrāt
adhovaktraparyantaṃ prāṇaśaktibrahmāśrayamadhyamanāḍīrūpatayā
prādhānyena sthitā | tata eva sarvavṛttīnām udayāt tatraiva ca viśrāmāt |
evaṃbhūtāpy eṣā paśūnāṃ nimīlitasvarūpaiva sthitā |
yadā tu uktayuktikrameṇa sarvāntaratamatve [21] madhyabhūtā saṃvid
bhagavatī vikasati yadi vā vakṣyamāṇakrameṇa madhyabhūtā brahmanāḍī
vikasati tadā tadvikāsāc cidānandasya uktarūpasya lābhaḥ prāptiḥ bhavati =
|
tataś ca prāg uktā jīvanmuktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) exists as the most inward of all [things], and since without being based on it (<s>tadbhittilagnatā</s>) no thing whatsoever can have its own essential nature, the blessed awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) itself is the 'center' (<s>madhya</s>). Now, She, though of such a nature even at the level of <s>Māyā</s>, having concealed Her essential nature — in accordance with [the principle that] 'consciousness first transforms into <s>prāṇa-śakti</s> (the power of vital breath)' — having assumed the level of <s>prāṇa-śakti</s>, [She] rests, through the process of descent, upon the plane of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), body, etc., following the path of the thousands of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels). And even there, by the principle of the middle branch of the <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest) leaf, She abides predominantly in the form of the central <s>nāḍī</s> — the <s>Brahma-āśraya</s> (support of <s>Brahman</s>) of the <s>prāṇa-śakti</s> — from the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (aperture at the crown) down to the lower opening — since all activities arise from there and come to rest there. Though of such a nature, this [awareness] remains in bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) with its essential nature closed. But when the blessed awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), which is the center — the most inward of all — expands through the previously stated method of reasoning; or when the central <s>Brahma-nāḍī</s> expands through the method to be stated — then, through that expansion, there is the attainment — the obtaining — of the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda</s>) of the nature described. And from that, the previously stated living liberation (<s>jīvanmukti</s>) [follows]. ||

children.text: madhyavikāse yuktim āha
children.translated_text: He states the method for the expansion of the center:

children.text: vikalpakṣayaśaktisaṃkocavikāsavāhacchedādyantakoṭinibhālanādaya
iha upāyāḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: these are the means (<s>upāyas</s>) here. || Sūtra 18 ||

The cessation of thought-constructs (<s>vikalpa-kṣaya</s>), the contraction and expansion of <s>Śakti</s>, the cutting of the flow [of breath] (<s>vāha-ccheda</s>), the contemplation of the beginning and ending points (<s>ādyanta-koṭi-nibhālana</s>), and the like —

children.text:
iha madhyaśaktivikāse vikalpakṣayādaya upāyāḥ |
prāgupadiṣṭapañcavidhakṛtyakāritvādyanusaraṇena sarvamadhyabhūtāyāḥ
saṃvido vikāso jāyata ity abhihitaprāyam | upāyāntaram api tu ucyate
prāṇāyāmamudrābandhādisamastayantraṇātantratroṭanena sukhopāyam eva
hṛdaye nihitacittaḥ uktayuktyā svasthitipratibandhakaṃ vikalpaṃ
akiṃciccintakatvena praśamayan avikalpaparāmarśena
dehādyakaluṣasvacitpramātṛtānibhālanapravaṇaḥ acirād eva
unmiṣadvikāsāṃ turyaturyātītasamāveśadaśāṃ āsādayati |
yathoktam=20
children.translated_text: Here, the cessation of thought-constructs etc. are the means for the expansion of the central power (<s>madhya-śakti</s>). By following [the recognition of] the previously taught authorship of the five acts and the like, the expansion of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) — which is the center of everything — arises. This has essentially been stated [already]. But another method is also taught: having placed the mind in the heart — [which is itself] an easy means, through the severing of all bondage-devices of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), <s>mudrā</s> (seals), <s>bandha</s> (locks), and the like — by pacifying through the state of thinking-of-nothing the thought-constructs that obstruct one's natural abiding, by the method previously stated, [and] being inclined through concept-free awareness (<s>avikalpa-parāmarśa</s>) toward the contemplation of one's own consciousness-knower uncontaminated by body etc. — one quickly arrives at the state of <s>samāveśa</s> (immersion) of <s>turya</s> (the fourth state) and <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), whose expansion is just about to unfold. As stated:

children.text: vikalpahānenaikāgryāt krameṇeśvaratāpadam [22] |
children.translated_text: 'Through the cessation of thought-constructs, through one-pointedness, progressively [one attains] the state of the Lord.' //

children.text: iti śrīpratyabhijñāyām |
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>.

children.text: śrīspande 'pi=20
children.translated_text: In the venerable <s>Spanda</s> [śāstra] also:

children.text: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syāt paramaṃ padam [23] | iti |
children.translated_text: 'When agitation dissolves, then the supreme state [arises].' //

children.text: śrījñānagarbhe 'pi
children.translated_text: In the venerable <s>Jñānagarbha</s> also:

children.text:
vihāya sakalāḥ kriyā janani mānasīḥ sarvato
vimuktakaraṇakriyānusṛtipāratantryojjvalam |
sthitais tvadanubhāvataḥ sapadi vedyate sā parā
daśā nṛbhir atandritāsamasukhāmṛtasyandinī || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned all mental activities, O Mother, everywhere, free from the dependence of following the activities of the sense-organs, radiant — by those who abide through Your grace, there is immediately known that supreme state, by attentive people — [that state which is] a flow of the nectar of supreme bliss.' //

children.text:
ayaṃ ca upāyo mūrdhanyatvāt pratyabhijñāyāṃ [24] pratipāditatvāt ādāv
uktaḥ | śaktisaṃkocādayas tu yady api pratyabhijñāyāṃ na pratipāditāḥ
tathāpi āmnāyikatvāt asmābhiḥ prasaṅgāt pradarśyante | bahuṣu hi
pradarśiteṣu kaścit kenacit pravekṣyatīti | śakteḥ saṃkoca
indriyadvāreṇa prasarantyā evākuñcanakrameṇa unmukhīkaraṇam | yathoktaṃ
ātharvaṇikopaniṣatsu kaṭhavallyāṃ caturthavallīprathamamantre
children.translated_text: And this method, being of the highest order, since it has been expounded in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, is stated first. But the contraction of <s>śakti</s> (power) etc., although not expounded in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, since they belong to the <s>Āgamic</s> tradition, are shown by us in this connection. For when many [methods] are shown, someone will enter [the path] through some [particular method]. The contraction of <s>śakti</s>: the making inward-facing through the gradual withdrawal of [the power] which extends outward through the gateway of the senses. As stated in the <s>Ātharvaṇika Upaniṣads</s>, in the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s>, in the first mantra of the fourth section —

children.text:
parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūḥ
tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman |
kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad
āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam aśnan [25] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The Self-Born (<s>Svayambhū</s>) pierced the openings [of the senses] outward; therefore one sees outward, not the inner Self. But a certain wise one, with inverted gaze, desiring immortality, beheld the inner Self.' //

children.text:
prasṛtāyā api vā kūrmāṅgasaṃkocavat trāsasamaye hṛtpraveśavac ca
sarvato nivartanam | yathoktaṃ "tadapoddhṛte nityoditasthitiḥ" iti |
śakter vikāsaḥ antarnigūḍhāyā akramam eva sakalakaraṇacakravisphāraṇen=
a
"antarlakṣyo bahirdṛṣṭiḥ nimeṣonmeṣavarjitaḥ " iti |
bhairavīyamudrānupraveśayuktyā bahiḥ prasaraṇam | yathoktaṃ
kakṣyastotre=20
children.translated_text: Or, even when [the power] has extended outward, [there is] the withdrawal from all [directions], like the contraction of a tortoise's limbs, or like the entering into the heart at the moment of fright. As stated: 'When that is withdrawn, there is the state of the ever-arisen.' The expansion (<s>vikāsa</s>) of <s>śakti</s>: of [the power] hidden within, the non-sequential opening out of the entire wheel of the senses — [as described]: 'The inner gaze, the outer vision, free from closing and opening of the eyes' — through the method of entering into the <s>Bhairavī mudrā</s> (the seal of the Fearsome Goddess), the extension outward. As stated in the <s>Kakṣyāstotra</s> —

children.text:
sarvāḥ śaktīḥ cetasā darśanādyāḥ
sve sve vedye yaugapadyena viṣvak |
kṣiptvā madhye hāṭakastambhabhūtaḥ
tiṣṭan viśvādhāra eko 'vabhāsi || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Having cast all the powers — consciousness, seeing, etc. — simultaneously and in all directions, each upon its own object, standing in the middle like a pillar of gold, you shine forth as the sole support of the universe!' //

children.text:
śrībhaṭṭakallaṭenāpi uktam "rūpādiṣu pariṇāmāt tatsiddhiḥ " iti |
śakteś ca saṃkocavikāsau
nāsāpuṭaspandanakramonmiṣatsūkṣmaprāṇaśaktyā bhrūbhedanena
kramāsāditordhvakuṇḍalinīpade prasaraviśrāntidaśāpariśīlanam |
adhaḥkuṇḍalinyāṃ ca ṣaṣṭavaktrarūpāyāṃ praguṇīkṛtya śaktiṃ
tanmūlatadagratanmadhyabhūmisparśāveśaḥ | yathoktaṃ vijñānabhaṭṭārake
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s> also said: 'Through transformation in [objects such as] form etc., that attainment [results].' The contraction and expansion of <s>śakti</s> [together]: by means of the subtle <s>prāṇaśakti</s> (vital power) that awakens through the sequential vibration of the nostrils — the cultivation of the stages of extension and rest in the station of the upper <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> gradually reached through the piercing of the eyebrow-center. And in the lower <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, which has the form of the six-mouthed [fire] — having straightened the <s>śakti</s>, the immersion through touching the ground at its root, its tip, and its middle. As stated in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> —

children.text:
vahner viṣasya madhye tu cittaṃ sukhamayaṃ kṣipet |
kevalaṃ vāyupūrṇaṃ vā smarānandena yujyate [26] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'One should cast the mind, filled with bliss, into the middle of fire and poison. Or [when it is] filled with breath alone, one becomes united with the bliss of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love).' //

children.translated_text: Here 'fire' is the ground of contraction through the method of inward entering. The place of 'poison' is the station of expansion through the method of extension — from the etymological understanding of 'viṣ' meaning 'to pervade.' Of the two currents (<s>vāhas</s>), left and right, of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — the cutting, preceded by resting in the heart, through the utterance of vowelless consonants predominantly consisting of 'ka,' 'ha,' etc. internally. As stated in the <s>Jñānagarbha</s> —

anackakakṛtāyatiprasṛtapārśvanāḍīdvayacchido

children.translated_text: 'Through the cutting of the two side channels, extended by the elongation effected by vowelless 'ka,' for one whose mind is held in the interior of the heart-lotus, there arises the sprout of knowledge, having shattered the darkness — this indeed is sufficient to generate the state of the Supreme Lord even for a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).' //

children.translated_text: The initial point (<s>ādikoṭi</s>) is the heart. The final point (<s>antakoṭi</s>) is the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the point twelve finger-breadths above the head). The cultivation through the directing of the mind at the occasions of the efflorescence and repose of <s>prāṇa</s> at those [two points], through the settling of consciousness. As stated in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> —

children.text:
hṛdyākāśe nilīnākṣaḥ padmasaṃpuṭamadhyagaḥ |
ananyacetāḥ subhage paraṃ saubhāgyam āpnuyāt [27] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'With eyes absorbed in the space of the heart, [seated] in the middle of a lotus-cup, with mind directed to nothing else — O beautiful one, one attains supreme good fortune!' //

children.translated_text: 'That should be known as <s>unmeṣa</s> (the opening of consciousness); one should discern it by oneself.' //

tathā ramaṇīyaviṣayacarvaṇādayaś ca saṃgṛhītāḥ |

children.translated_text: Likewise, the savoring of delightful objects etc. are also included. As stated in the venerable <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> itself —

children.text: jagdhipānakṛtollāsarasānandavijṛmbhaṇāt |
children.translated_text: 'From the exhilaration produced by eating and drinking, from the expansion of the delight of that savor,

children.text: bhāvayed bharitāvasthāṃ mahānandamayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should contemplate the state of fullness — one becomes filled with great bliss.' //

children.translated_text: 'For the yogin whose being is of the nature of the one bliss equal to the relishing of objects such as song etc.,

children.text: yoginas tanmayatvena manorūḍhes tadātmatā ||

children.translated_text: 'Wherever the mind finds satisfaction, one should hold the mind right there. In every such [experience], the nature of supreme bliss shines forth.' //

children.text:
evam anyad api ānandapūrṇasvātmabhāvanādikaṃ anumantavyam | ity
evamādayaḥ atra madhyavikāse upāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus other [methods] too — such as the contemplation of one's own Self as full of bliss — should be inferred. These and similar [practices] are the methods for the expansion of the center (<s>madhyavikāsa</s>). ||

children.text:
madhyavikāsāc cidānandalābhaḥ | sa eva ca paramayoginaḥ
samāveśasamapattyādiparyāyaḥ samādhiḥ | tasya nityoditatve yuktim āha
children.translated_text: From the expansion of the center (<s>madhyavikāsa</s>), the attainment of the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda</s>). That alone, for the supreme yogin, is <s>samādhi</s> — synonymous with <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment), etc. In order to state the means for its becoming perpetually arisen (<s>nityodita</s>), he says —

children.text: samādhisaṃskāravati vyutthāne bhūyo bhūyaḥ
cidaikyāmarśān nityoditasamādhilābhaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: through repeated and continuous awareness of the unity with consciousness (<s>cidaikya</s>), there is the attainment of perpetually-arisen <s>samādhi</s>. || Sūtra 19 ||
In the emergent state (<s>vyutthāna</s>) [that follows] one endowed with the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text:
āsāditasamāveśo yogivaro vyutthāne 'pi samādhirasasaṃskāreṇa kṣība iva
sānandaṃ ghūrṇamāno bhāvarāśiṃ śaradabhralavaṃ iva cidgagana eva
līyamānaṃ paśyan bhūyo bhūyaḥ antarmukhatāṃ eva samavalambamāno
nimīlanasamādhikrameṇa cidaikyam eva vimṛśan vyutthānābhimatāvasare 'pi
samādhyekarasa eva bhavati | yathoktaṃ kramasūtreṣu
children.translated_text: The excellent yogin who has attained <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), even in the emergent state (<s>vyutthāna</s>), as if intoxicated by the savor of the impressions of <s>samādhi</s>, blissfully swaying, seeing the mass of [objective] existence dissolving in the sky of consciousness like a fragment of autumn cloud, again and again resorting to inward-orientation alone, through the sequence of <s>nimilana-samādhi</s> (closed-eyed absorption) contemplating the unity with consciousness alone — even at the occasion deemed to be the emergent state, he remains of the single savor of <s>samādhi</s> alone. As stated in the <s>Kramasūtras</s> —

children.text:
"kramamudrayā antaḥsvarūpayā bahirmukhaḥ [31] samāviṣṭo bhavati
sādhakaḥ |
tatrādau bāhyāt antaḥpraveśaḥ ābhyantarāt bāhyasvarūpe praveśaḥ
āveśavaśāt jāyate iti sabāhyābhyantaro 'yaṃ mudrākramaḥ " iti |
children.translated_text: 'Through <s>kramamudrā</s> (the seal of the sequence), which has the nature of the inner essential form, the practitioner becomes absorbed even while outward-facing. Therein, first there is entry inward from the external; then, from the internal, entry into the external form occurs due to the force of absorption. Thus this <s>mudrākrama</s> (seal-sequence) is both external and internal.' //

paramānandasvarūpatvāt pāśadrāvaṇāt viśvasya antaḥturīyasattāyāṃ
children.translated_text: because of being of the nature of supreme bliss, because it melts the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), because it seals the universe in the inner state of <s>Turīyā</s> (the Fourth),

children.text: mudraṇāt ca mudrātmā kramo 'pi sṛṣṭyādikramābhāsakatvāt
children.translated_text: it is of the nature of <s>mudrā</s> (seal). It is called <s>krama</s> (sequence) because it causes the appearance of the sequence of creation etc.,

children.text: tatkramābhāsarūpatvāt ca krama iti abhidhīyata iti ||
children.translated_text: and because it is of the nature of the appearance of that sequence — thus it is called [<s>kramamudrā</s>]. ||

Here the meaning is: that which seals (<s>mudrayati</s>) — makes one's own, establishes in oneself — the sequence (<s>krama</s>) that is of the nature of the wheel of the consciousness of creation, maintenance, and dissolution: this is the <s>Turīyā</s> (Fourth) <s>citi-śakti</s> (power of consciousness). By that <s>kramamudrā</s>, 'inward' means of the nature of the full 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>); 'outward-facing' means even while engaged in objects — 'absorbed' means having directly realized the expansion of the supreme <s>Śakti</s> — the practitioner, the supreme yogin, becomes [so]. And therein, from the external — from the mass of objects being consumed — inward, into the ground of supreme consciousness (<s>citi</s>), entry through the very method of consuming is <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption). And from the internal — from the essential nature of <s>citiśakti</s> directly realized — due to the force of absorption, by the very power of absorption, entry into the external form, into the mass of objects appearing as 'this-ness' (<s>idantā</s>), through the method of emitting — the absorption that is the spreading of the savor of consciousness — arises. Thus this, both external and internal, of the nature of perpetually-arisen absorption (<s>nityoditasamāveśa</s>) — because it bestows joy (<s>mudā</s>), happiness,

children.text: idānīm asya samādhilābhasya phalam āha
children.translated_text: Now he states the fruit of this attainment of <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: tadā prakāśānandasāramahāmantravīryātmakapūrṇāhantāveśāt sadā
children.translated_text: Then, from the immersion in the full 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>) — whose essence is luminosity and bliss, which is of the nature of the power of the Great Mantra (<s>mahāmantra-vīrya</s>) — always,

children.text: sarvasargasaṃhārakārinijasaṃviddevatācakreśvaratāpraptir
children.translated_text: there is the attainment of Lordship over the wheel of one's own consciousness-deities (<s>saṃviddevatācakra</s>), which effects the creation and dissolution of everything —

children.text: bhavatīti śivam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: this is <s>Śiva</s>. || Sūtra 20 ||

children.translated_text: When the perpetually-arisen <s>samādhi</s> has been attained, the 'I'-consciousness — whose essence is luminosity and bliss, a single mass of the delight of consciousness (<s>cidāhlāda</s>), great, of the nature of the power of all mantras' life-force (<s>mantravīrya</s>), full, of the form of the Supreme Sovereign (<s>Parābhaṭṭārikā</s>), an unartificial wonder of one's own Self — from the immersion in that, always: of the universe from <s>Kālāgni</s> (the Fire of Time) to the final <s>kalā</s> (phase), the wondrous creation and dissolution, the varied emission and withdrawal — [of the wheel of] consciousness-deities (<s>saṃviddevatācakra</s>) that is one's own and that effects these — the attainment, the reaching, of the lordship of that [wheel] occurs. This means: for the supreme yogin who is the subject of this [treatise]. The concluding synthesis (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) is: all this is indeed the essential nature of <s>Śiva</s> — this is the connection. Therein: whatever is cognized — its cognition itself is its essential nature. And the subjects (<s>pramātṛs</s>, knowing agents) who are of the nature of inward-facing reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) — they are the <s>tattva</s> (reality) [of that cognition]. And for them, when the false identification with limitations such as the body etc. has fallen away, when the body is all bodies — the essence is indeed the Lordship of <s>Sadāśiva-Īśvara</s>. And of that [Lordship] too, the glorious <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord) — who is the wonder of the entire universe established by the sole reality of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) — is alone the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). For without the immersion in the real luminosity (<s>pāramārthika-prakāśa</s>), the luminousness of anything whatever is not possible. And that Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), being of the essence of absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), by virtue of being of the nature of the reflective awareness of the entire mass of <s>Māyīya</s> words from 'a' to 'kṣa' — because He establishes the blissful existence of the entire world consisting of all signifiers and signifieds that He has thus made His own — is supremely full (<s>paripūrṇa</s>), and therefore, being free from all want, He overflows with the effusion of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>). For this very reason, from the 'a'-sound — which is of the nature of <s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassed) and <s>Akula</s> (the Transcendent) — up to the 'ha'-<s>kalā</s> (phase), which is the form of the expansion of <s>Śakti</s>: whatever universe has been emitted — since the 'kṣa'-sound has the nature of the calming of emission — that [universe], by the very method of being enclosed (<s>saṃpuṭīkāra</s>) between 'a' and 'ha,' through the principle of withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), having been internally appropriated, having flashed forth in the form of <s>Bindu</s> (the Point) — which is of the nature of the awareness of non-difference — comes to rest in <s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassed) alone. Thus this reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), which is of the very nature of the mass of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>), is unartificial. As stated —

children.text: prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The repose of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) in the Self is indeed declared as the I-consciousness (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>);'

children.text: uktā ca saiva viśrāntiḥ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'And that very repose is said [to be called thus] because of the cessation of all dependence —'

children.text: svātantryam atha kartṛtvaṃ mukhyam īśvaratāpi ca [34] | iti |
children.translated_text: '[It is] absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), and primary agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), and also lordship (<s>īśvaratā</s>).'

eṣaiva ca ahantā sarvamantrāṇāṃ udayaviśrāntisthānatvāt etadbalenaiva c=

children.translated_text: And this very I-consciousness, being the place of arising and repose for all <s>mantras</s>, and because all respective purposeful activities are accomplished by its power, is the great ground of power (<s>vīryabhūmi</s>). As it is stated —

children.text: tadākramya balaṃ mantrā ..... | ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Having attained that power, <s>mantras</s> ...' and so forth,

children.translated_text: '... they become possessed of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.' — thus it concludes in the revered <s>Spandakārikā</s>.

children.translated_text: Therefore, here, immersion (<s>āveśa</s>) in the full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>), which is of the nature of the great <s>mantra</s>-power — through the submergence of body, vital breath, and the rest, and through firm establishment in that state — [results in] the saturation of the body and the rest, and even of blue and the like, with its essence, making them one with that [consciousness]. For whatever is manifested — body, pleasure, blue, etc. — whether it is cognized, ascertained, remembered, or imagined — in all of that, the divine expansion (<s>prathā</s>), consisting of the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), shines as the underlying ground (<s>bhittibhūta</s>). 'Because without its shining, nothing at all shines' — as it has been stated. Only, even though she shines thus, due to the assumption of identification imposed by the coloring of body, blue, and the like manifested by her <s>māyā</s>-power, she appears as if of divided and differentiated nature, and is [mistakenly] considered by the <s>māyā</s>-experiencers in the forms of cognition, imagination, ascertainment, and the rest. But in reality, she is the one power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) alone. As stated —

akramānantacidrūpaḥ pramātā sa maheśvaraḥ [37] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'That very flash (<s>pratibhā</s>) — adorned by the sequence of various objects — the perceiver who is of the nature of non-sequential, infinite consciousness is the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>).'

children.translated_text: 'That very [power], through the <s>māyā</s>-<s>śakti</s> of the all-pervading Lord, whose domain is differentiated objects, is called by the names: cognition, imagination, ascertainment, and the rest.'
