tadanupraveśatadavaṣṭambhayuktyā samāsādyate tat tadāveśāt
pūrvoktayuktyā karaṇonmīlananimīlanakrameṇa sarvasya sarvamayatvāt
tattatsaṃhārādau api sadā sarvasargasaṃhārakāri yat
sahajasaṃvittidevatācakraṃ amāyīyāntarbahiṣkaraṇamarīcipuñjaḥ tatra
īśvaratāsāmrajyaṃ parabhairavātmatā tatprāptiḥ bhavati
paramayoginaḥ | yathoktam
children.translated_text: Thus, this one power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>), expanding through all states, if it is attained through the method of entering into it and firmly establishing oneself in it, then — through that immersion, by the previously stated method, through the sequence of opening and closing of the faculties — since everything is constituted of everything, even in the dissolution etc. of any particular [thing], the innate wheel of the goddess of consciousness (<s>sahaja-saṃvittidevatācakra</s>), which is always the agent of the creation and dissolution of all, the cluster of rays of the non-<s>māyic</s> inner and outer faculties — in that, there is the sovereignty of lordship (<s>īśvaratā</s>), the identity with <s>Parabhairava</s> (the Supreme <s>Bhairava</s>), the attainment of that — for the supreme <s>yogin</s>. As stated —

children.text:
yadā tv ekatra saṃrūḍhas tadā tasya layodbhavau |
niyacchan bhoktṛtām eti tataś cakreśvaro bhavet [39] || iti |
children.translated_text: 'But when one has become firmly established in one [center of consciousness], then, controlling the arising and dissolution of that [puryaṣṭaka], one attains the status of the experiencer, and thereby becomes the Lord of the Wheel (<s>Cakreśvara</s>).'

children.text:
atra ekatra iti "ekatrāropayet sarvaṃ" [40] iti citsāmānyaspandabhūḥ
unmeṣātmā vyākhyātavyā |
tasya iti anena "puryaṣṭakena saṃruddha" [41] iti | upakrāntaṃ
puryaṣṭakam eva parāmraṣṭavyam na tu yathā vivaraṇakṛtaḥ ekatra
sūkṣme sthūle śarīre vā iti vyākṛtavantaḥ | stutaṃ ca mayā
children.translated_text: Here, 'in one' should be explained as the ground of the <s>spanda</s> (vibration) of the universal consciousness, having the nature of <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening/expansion), as in [the verse] 'One should deposit everything in one [center].' By 'of that,' it is the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) itself that is to be grasped, as introduced in [the verse] 'constricted by the subtle body' — not as the commentators have explained [it] as 'in one subtle or gross body.' And I have praised [this] —

children.text:
svatantraś citicakrāṇāṃ cakravartī maheśvaraḥ |
saṃvittidevatācakrajuṣṭaḥ ko 'pi jayaty asau || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The autonomous Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), the sovereign of the wheels of consciousness (<s>citicakra</s>), endowed with the wheel of the goddesses of consciousness (<s>saṃvittidevatācakra</s>) — victorious is that certain Indescribable One!'

children.text:
itiśabda upasaṃhāre | yat etāvat uktaprakaraṇaśarīraṃ tat sarvaṃ
śivaṃ śivaprāptihetutvāt śivāt prasṛtatvāt śivasvarūpābhinnatvāc ca
śivamayam eva iti śivam |
children.translated_text: The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) serves as a conclusion. All that has been stated as the body of this treatise — all that is <s>Śiva</s>: because it is the cause of attaining <s>Śiva</s>, because it has issued forth from <s>Śiva</s>, and because it is non-different from <s>Śiva</s>'s own nature — it is entirely of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. Thus, auspiciousness (<s>śivam</s>).

children.text: dehaprāṇasukhādibhiḥ pratikalaṃ saṃrudhyamāno janaḥ
children.translated_text: People, constantly constrained at every moment by body, vital breath, pleasure, and the rest,

children.text: pūrṇānandaghanām imāṃ na cinute māheśvarīṃ svāṃ citim |
children.translated_text: do not perceive this sovereign power of consciousness (<s>māheśvarī citi</s>), which is their own, a solid mass of perfect bliss.

children.text: madhyebodhasudhābdhi viśvam abhitas tatphenapiṇḍopamaṃ
children.translated_text: Whoever sees the universe as a lump of foam, as it were, [floating] everywhere in the midst of the ocean of the nectar of awakening (<s>bodhasudhābdhi</s>) —

children.text: yaḥ paśyed upadeśatas tu kathitaḥ sākṣāt sa ekaḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he, through [proper] instruction, is directly proclaimed as the one <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yeṣāṃ vṛttaḥ śāṅkaraḥ śaktipāto
children.translated_text: For those upon whom has descended the <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva's) descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>),

children.text: ye 'nabhyāsāt tīkṣṇayuktiṣv ayogyāḥ |
children.translated_text: who are unfit for sharp reasoning due to lack of practice,

children.text: śaktā jñātuṃ neśvarapratyabhijñām
children.translated_text: [yet are] capable of knowing the Recognition of the Lord (<s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>) —

children.text: uktas teṣām eṣa tattvopadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for them, this teaching of reality (<s>tattvopadeśa</s>) has been spoken.

children.text:
samāptam idaṃ pratyabhijñāhṛdayam kṛtis
tatrabhavanmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryaśrīmadabhinavaguptapādapadmopajīvinaḥ
śrīmato rājānakakṣemarājācaryasya
children.translated_text: This <s>Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam</s> (The Heart of Recognition) is completed. It is the composition of the revered <s>Rājānaka Kṣemarāja</s>, who subsists upon the lotus-feet of the great master (<s>mahāmāheśvarācāryavarya</s>), the glorious <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

children.text: śubham astu
children.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness (<s>śubham astu</s>).
